findings.title: Shell-command blanket catch and unchecked `shell()` results in cutover steps
findings.description: `run_health`, `step_offsite` and `step_metadata` call `shell(...)`, which uses `subprocess.run` without `check`. In `run_health` and `step_offsite` the return code is dropped. A failed health command is only caught indirectly, when the last log line has no FLAGS summary. That line could be stale from an earlier run, so a failed health run could pass on an old log line. Also, `step_offsite` ignores the push command's exit code and relies only on `rclone check`. Check the exit code, or record the log's mtime or length before the run and compare afterwards.

findings.title: Fragile `assert` used as control flow in production script
findings.description: `block_commands` has `assert match is not None`, and `run_health` has `assert flags is not None`. Both are stripped under `python -O`, and the first one would surface as an unhelpful AssertionError rather than a `StepFailed`. Raise `StepFailed` explicitly. The `job_lines` regex also anchors on exactly five whitespace-separated fields. That is fine for the current template but misparses `@reboot` style lines.

findings.title: Stale-weekly skip heuristic can arm an unverified cluster
findings.description: The skip condition is "a base dir named for today exists and the arm file exists". It does not check that the base backup completed. A partial directory left by an interrupted run, plus an arm file, makes a re-run skip verification. The directory and arm file are also only a same-day check, so the step cannot be re-validated the next day. Consider tying the skip to the weekly log's done line.

findings.title: Arm-file touch happens before offsite verification and is not reversible by re-run
findings.description: The step arms reconciliation, which is destructive pruning, at step 8, before steps 10 to 12 verify health and offsite parity. If a later step fails, the cluster stays armed. The report says to fix and re-run, but the arm file persists and the reconcile guard is then live. Consider arming only after verification passes, or documenting that explicitly.

findings.title: `PUSH_MIN_AGE_S` coupling duplicates a constant owned by another script
findings.description: The value 120 mirrors `MIN_AGE` inside `sync_wal_offsite.sh`, and `WEEKLY_DONE` mirrors a log string in `cron_weekly_backup.sh`. Two definitions drift silently. Per the project's "one value, one place" rule, read them from the owning script or a shared constants file.

findings.title: Lifecycle output parsing and prefixing rely on string matching
findings.description: `run_lib` rewrites status lines with a `sed` over the exact words `OK|DRIFT|MISSING|...`. The lifecycle loop re-parses the same lines by prefix, and `setup_not_ok` in Python re-parses them again by regex. The status vocabulary is therefore defined in three places. The `--rehearse` and `MISSING <cluster> lifecycle` conventions are tested, but a new status word would be silently dropped from tallies. Centralize the vocabulary.

findings.title: Python tooling configuration not verifiable; new scripts import via `sys.path` hack with `noqa: E402`
findings.description: The script inserts `scripts/` into `sys.path` and silences E402 on every import. It also imports `backup_clusters` and `cutover_common`, which I could not inspect. The rules require strict pyright and the ruff select list (`BLE`, `ASYNC`, `B`, and others) in `pyproject.toml`. I could not confirm that the new files are covered or clean under them. The `_load` helper in the tests repeats the same path hack.

findings.title: Tests assert script source text rather than behavior
findings.description: Several new tests regex-extract shell source and compare literal strings. Examples are `test_parent_directories_755_data_directory_700`, `test_only_trading_tick_is_created` and `test_roles_are_applied_with_replication`. They fail on harmless refactors and do not prove that REPLICATION is granted or that pg_hba admits replication. `test_roles_sql_grants_replication_only_when_asked` only checks the ordering of two substrings. Run the SQL against a throwaway database, or exercise the function with stubs.

findings.title: No load test for the new cluster loops
findings.description: The change touches the backup and network paths, but no `tests/load/` tier was added. That fits one-off host tooling, so I am recording it only as an observation.

findings.title: Good practices observed
findings.description:
- The lifecycle checker is read-only by design, and the comment explains why: `rclone backend lifecycle` replaces all rules.
- The `render_cron.sh` replacements quote the replacement text to avoid bash 5.2 `&` expansion, and this is tested.
- The cluster table is parsed before any step runs, which is also tested.
- The cutover stops at the first failed step and still writes its report.

structured_findings.summary: Shell-command blanket catch and unchecked `shell()` results in cutover steps
Fragile `assert` used as control flow in production script
Stale-weekly skip heuristic can arm an unverified cluster
Arm-file touch happens before offsite verification and is not reversible by re-run
`PUSH_MIN_AGE_S` coupling duplicates a constant owned by another script
Lifecycle output parsing and prefixing rely on string matching
Python tooling configuration not verifiable; new scripts import via `sys.path` hack with `noqa: E402`
Tests assert script source text rather than behavior
No load test for the new cluster loops
